claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr suffers significant oxygen-induced degradation at high temperatures.
Pack aluminization will introduce aluminum into the surface of HfNbTaTiZr by diffusion.
Pack aluminization followed by high-temperature oxygen exposure will form a continuous, thin Al2O3 layer on HfNbTaTiZr.
The resulting Al2O3 layer will be adherent to the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
A continuous Al2O3 surface layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Limiting oxygen ingress will prevent internal oxidation of HfNbTaTiZr during high-temperature exposure.
Preventing internal oxidation will preserve the bulk microstructure responsible for the alloy's useful mechanical properties.
After 100 hours at 1000 °C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere or air, aluminized specimens will have lower oxygen uptake than untreated specimens.
After 100 hours at 1000 °C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere or air, aluminized specimens will exhibit less surface oxidation than untreated specimens.
Aluminized specimens will retain room-temperature tensile ductility comparable to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Aluminized specimens will retain 1000 °C yield strength comparable to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The intervention is effective only when the aluminization treatment avoids altering the alloy's bulk microstructure.
Substantial changes in aluminization temperature, duration, or powder composition may degrade mechanical performance.
